svg.aria-label: Two grouped bar panels comparing a closed frontier model against an open-weight model on capability versus safety, based on SaferAI's August 4 2026 report. Left panel, offensive cyber and biology capability: the closed frontier reference (Claude Opus 4.7 / GPT-5.5) is near the top of the scale at about 95 percent, and the open-weight GLM-5.2 is nearly level at about 88 percent, only a few months behind. Right panel, share of harmful prompts refused: the closed frontier model refused so consistently that the CyberGym benchmark could not be completed, shown near 100 percent, while the open-weight model refused essentially zero percent, completing every offensive cyber and dual-use biology prompt. The visual shows near-parity on capability but an almost total gap on safety.
svg.title: The capability gap closed; the safety gap didn't — open-weight models now match the frontier on cyber/bio ability but refuse almost none of the harmful prompts a closed model refuses
svg.text: Same ability, opposite guardrails — the open-weight safety gap (SaferAI, Aug 4)

Open-weight GLM-5.2 sits within a few months of the closed frontier on offensive cyber/bio capability — yet refuses almost none of the harmful prompts a closed model refuses. Slate = closed frontier (Claude Opus 4.7 / GPT-5.5); teal = open weight (GLM-5.2).
"only a few months behind" GPT-5.5 & Opus 4.7
Opus 4.7 refused so hard CyberGym couldn't run; GLM-5.2 refused none

Capability bars are indicative of SaferAI's "few months behind" framing (UK AISI cyber range: GLM-5.2 ≈ Opus 4.5); refusal bars are qualitative from SaferAI (open: 0 refusals; closed: CyberGym incompletable). Not a single common numeric scale across both panels.
